why: RJ-X49 (suiteui/adopt-kernel-eyedropper-photo, written by EP-1, its Model check turns on with EP-2): opens a 16 x 16 checkerboard of 4 x 4 cells of pure red and pure blue (red where the cell's column + row is even, so the top-left cell is red), the harness's file.open of the input, picks the Eyedropper with tool.eyedropper, samples a 5 x 5 square at the corner (0, 0) and then at the centre (8, 8) with color.sample, and exports the PNG. The trap: Photo's own square math counts the off-image pixels of the corner square as black, so the corner reads darker than the kernel's mean. The assertion: the corner is the mean of its 9 in-image pixels, #FF0000; the centre is the 25-pixel mean, 13 red and 12 blue, #85007A; both equal SampleRules.mean's hex; the export is the input unchanged.
